content.title: NCAA Wrestling championships: Penn State claims four individual titles
content.text: March 21, 2026Updated March 22, 2026, 7:30 a.m. ETPenn State wrestling has already added another national championship trophy to the collection on Saturday at the NCAA Wrestling Championships in Cleveland, Ohio, but the Nittany Lions are hoping to add a few more titles to the collection this evening. The Nittany Lions and head coach Cael Sanderson clinched the team national championship earlier in the day with consolation match performances by Marcus Blaze and PJ Duke, and the dominance is expected to continue in the finals on Saturday evening.Penn State will have six No. 1 seeds in the finals with Luke Lilledahl (125), Shayne Van Ness (149), Mitchell Messenbrink (165), Levi Haines (174), Rocco Welsh (184), and Josh Barr (197) all earning their places in the finals on Friday.We'll be providing live updates and reactions from the NCAA championship finals as Penn State chases more history for the program. Follow along with our live blog. Penn State brings home four individual national titles to go with team titleWith Luke Lilledahl claiming his national title, Penn State now has four individual national champions this year returning home to Happy Valley. And this brings a close to the wrestling season for the Nittany Lions, who are once again proving that when it comes to college wrestling, everyone else is just battling for second place. 125 lb: Luke Lilledahl wins defensive scrap to win national titlePenn State's Luke Lilledahl and Princeton's Marc-Anthony McGowan battled to a scoreless first round in their finals bout, but McGowan struck first with a point in the second round. That was the only point of the round, which sent Lilledahl into the third round trailing 1-0.Lilledahl quickly tied the match up with a point as the third round got underway. Lilledahl was awarded a second point for a second stalling infraction by McGowan, which gave the top-seeded Nittany Lion his first lead going into the final minute of the round. The two locked up, going to the ground in the final seconds, and the smile from Lilledahl started as the final seconds ticked away, as he knew he had a national championship coming his way. Penn State sets new NCAA championships team point totalWith Josh Barr's national championship victory, Penn State's overall team point total climbed to 177.5. That sets a new NCAA record for the most points in the NCAA championships. Fittingly, Penn State broke the mark previously set by Penn State with 177 points just last year. 197 lb: Josh Barr holds on for national championship, Penn State's third of the nightJosh Barr and No. 7-seed Cody Merrill went back and forth in the first round of their finals match without any scoring until a three-point takedown for Barr in the final 30 seconds of the round. A blood timeout with 13 seconds remaining gave each wrestler a chance to recover for the final push in the round. Merrill recorded a late point before the round ended, giving Barr a 3-1 lead going to the second round.Merrill picked up another quick point at the start of the second round with another quick escape. Barr took a 3-2 lead into the third round.As the third round began, Barr picked up a couple of points with a reversal and then added another point to take a 6-2 lead. Merrill rebounded with a quick point as the round continued. Up 6-3, Barr held off Merrill for the remainder of the round to clinch a national championship. 184 lb: Rocco Welsh upset by Minnesota's Max McEnellyTop-seed Rocco Welsh fell behind 3-0 to No. 3 seed Max McEnelly of Minnesota following a three-point takedown but quickly rebounded with a point before the end of the first round.McEnelly took a 4-1 lead in the second round with a quick escape and took that lead into the third round. Welsh had some work to do and started the third round on bottom, allowing him to pick up a quick point at the start of the round. Despite his best efforts to find an opening for a move, time ran out on Welsh as Minnesota's McEnelly pulled the upset with a 4-3 victory.McEnelly is the first national champion in the 184-lb weight division in school history. 174 lb: Levi Haines wins low-scoring bout for national titleA battle of Big Ten stars between Levi Haines and Nebraska's Christopher Minto opened with a scoreless first frame. Haines scored the first point of the match in the second round with a quick escape point. He doubled the lead with a second point later to take a 2-0 lead into the third round.Minto picked up a quick escape point at the start of the third round, but that would be all the scoring in a low-scoring finals match. Levi Haines is a national champion, making him the first wrestler to win national titles in two different weight classes. Shayne Van Ness was late to the award standIn case you were curious why Shayne Van Ness was running late... 165 lb: Mitchell Messenbrink dominates his way to the national championshipAfter a few upsets to get the night started, top-seed Mitchell Messenbrink came out ready to make sure he would not be the next upset victim. Messenbrink stormed out to a commanding 12-4 lead in the first round against Iowa's Mikey Caliendo, even with a cut on the head along the way.Messenbrink added to his lead with 6 more points in the second round to take an 18-4 lead into the third round. Messenbrink celebrated with a 20-4 victory with a tech fall to clinch the win. Messenbrink is now officially a back-to-back national champion. Oklahoma State gets second individual champion, Big Ten wrestlers 0-3 to start finalsWhat was expected to be a big night for Penn State wrestlers has started off as a headlining night for Oklahoma State. The Cowboys have two national champs in the first few bouts tonight after Sergio Vega (141) and Landon Robideau (157) each took home their championships.The Big Ten's top wrestlers so far have been on the wrong end of the finals bouts with Shayne Van Ness being joined by No. 1 Jesse Mendez of Ohio State and No. 2 Antrell Taylor of Nebraska as runners-up. 149 lb: Shayne Van Ness upset by Aden Valencia of StanfordThe top-seeded Shayne Van Ness was put in an early hole with a three-point takedown by Aden Valencia of Stanford. Penn State called for a coach's challenge but the review did not go Penn State's way.Van Ness managed to get a point back before the end of the first but found himself back in a three-point hole early in the second following a quick escape by Valencia. Van Ness tied it up with a three-point takedown of his own shortly after that. Valencia regained the lead with another quick escape point, which was followed by a blood timeout.Van Ness started off the third round on the bottom and quickly evened the score at 5-5. The two spent the majority of the rest of the round grabbing at ankles on the ground, leading to an overtime round.Valencia scored the upset with a three-point takedown, which was upheld after a coach's challenge by Penn State. This was the first loss of the year for Shayne Van Ness. This is the first wrestling title won by a wrestler from Stanford since 2021. Tonight's schedule for Penn State wrestlersShane Van Ness is the first Penn State wrestler in action in the finals this evening. His match is coming up shortly. ESPN will provide additional coverage with live streams of the action on each mat through ESPN+.Streaming options for the NCAA wrestling championships include ESPN+, the official streaming platform from ESPN, and Fubo, which comes with a free trial for new members.Watch NCAA Wrestling Championships on ESPN+Penn State clinches 2026 NCAA team championshipPenn State established a healthy lead in the overall team point totals through Friday's action, which put the Nittany Lions on the doorstep of its fifth-consecutive national championship. That national championship was clinched hours before the start of the championship finals when PJ Duke and Marcus Blaze were competing in the final rounds of the consolation matches and added to the overall point total. As a result of their performances, including Duke's third-place finish, no other team will be able to catch Penn State in the overall standings regardless of the results in the finals.Now, Penn State looks to run up the score and go home with even more reasons to celebrate.Penn State's NCAA Championship finals participantsHere is the full list of Penn State wrestlers in the NCAA championship finals for their respective weight classes, and what their championship match pairing will be. Marcusa Blaze (133) and PJ Duke (157) will compete in the consolation semifinals.125: No. 1 Luke Lilledahl vs. Marc-Anthony McGowan (Princeton)149: No. 1 Shayne Van Ness vs. No. 10 Aden Valencia (Stanford)165: No. 1 Mitchell Mesenbrink vs. No. 3 Mikey Caliendo (Iowa)174: No. 1 Levi Haines vs. No. 3 Christopher Minto (Nebraska)184: No. 1 Rocco Welsh vs. No. 3 Max McEnelly (Minnesota)197: No. 1 Josh Barr vs. No. 7 Cody Merrill (Oklahoma State)NCAA Overall point total through Session VKevin McGuire is the lead writer for Nittany Lions Wire.
